findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
(1) Observed several items in the sandwich meat prep cooler were not below 41°F, including: beef 47°F (probed), rotisserie chicken 49°F (probed), provolone 47°F (probed), cheddar 47°F (probed), turkey 47°F (probed), ham 47°F (probed), tuna 48°F (probed). CORRECTED: PIC voluntarily discarded these items, as they had been prepared longer than 4 hours previously, so they were not being controlled by either time or temperature. All other items that were sufficiently cold holding at or below 41°F were moved to the walk-in cooler.
(2) Observed sliced tomatoes in the short cooler was not below 41°F, and was measured at 52°F (probed). CORRECTED: PIC voluntarily discarded the tomatoes, as they had been prepared longer than 4 hours previously, so they were not being controlled by either time or temperature. All other items that were cold holding in the short cooler were moved to the walk-in cooler, as they were either not RTE, TCS, or had been prepared within 4 hours.
Ensure that RTE, TCS foods are cold held at 41°F or below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment:
(1) Observed that sandwich meat prep cooler was not holding proper temperatures for cold holding non-frozen foods. Temperatures were too warm, over 41°F (see #22). Staff reports that the prep cooler ices over when left running overnight (running too cold), so staff procedure to is store food in the walk-in cooler overnight and turn off the prep cooler, and then turn on the prep cooler in the morning and move the food from the walk-in to the prep cooler. PIC has placed a work order to fix the prep cooler.
(2) Observed that short counter cooler was not holding proper temperatures for cold holding non-frozen foods. Internal food temperatures were too warm, over 41°F (see #22). Ambient temperature was above 46°F. Please repair the short cooler so that it holds foods below 41°F.
Until coolers are repaired, staff will prepare smaller amounts of food and work out of the walk-in cooler. If items must be out of the walk-in cooler for a length of time, then staff will use time as a control: food will be used or discarded within 4 hours.
Inspector will Follow Up to confirm that prep cooler and short cooler are keeping proper cold-holding temperatures. Ensure that all cold holding equipment is sufficient to maintain foods at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Observed that establishment did not have a working probe-style thermometer available during the inspection. CORRECTED: PIC was able to borrow their neighboring establishment’s probe-style thermometer during the inspection, and located their own probe-style thermometer soon after the inspection had concluded. Ensure that a probe-styled thermometer is readily accessible to measure temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed several areas of the walk-in cooler where there was food residue and other debris on the floors. CORRECTED: Staff cleaned up the bottom of the walk-in coolers during the inspection. Ensure that nonfood-contact surfaces are kept free of an accumulation of food residue and debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a small floor tile missing right of the triple and mop sinks, as well as coving peeling from the wall (in the same area). Surfaces around floors and walls should be maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure these repairs occur before the next routine inspection to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed a mop that was stored on the floor, and not stored above the mop sink nor in the basket of the mop bucket where it can sufficiently air-dry. CORRECTED: PIC moved the mop during the inspection so that it will hang to air-dry over the mop sink. Ensure that mops can sufficiently air-dry between uses.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the food handler fail to wash hands when switching tasks between handling monetary transactions and preparing food. CORRECTED- the food handler washed their hands between tasks at the inspector’s bequest. Wash hands before donning gloves to prevent transferring pathogens from bare hands to gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: No sanitizer bucket was available at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) made a sanitizer bucket of quaternary ammonia at a concentration of 200 ppm. Sanitizer must be available for food contacts surfaces at all times food is being prepared or handled. Make sanitizer each day before food is handled or prepared, and remake throughout the day to maintain the proper concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: An accumulation of soil debris was observed around the drainage line in the walk in cooler. Routine cleaning should take place to prevent the accumulation of soil debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a small floor tile missing right of the triple and mop sinks, as well as coving peeling from the wall (in the same area). Surfaces around floors and walls should be maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure these repairs occur before the next routine inspection to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to dispensing paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Ensure proper handwashing between tasks.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12 Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Mold accumulation was observed in the walk-in cooler on the black pipe behind the fans and around the floor drain. Clean the walk-in cooler as frequently as needed to prevent soil/mold accumulation.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
No measurable Cl concentration observed in the SaniStation spray bottle near the meat slicer. CORRECTED- Employee indicated that sanitizer spray bottle had not been refreshed since the previous evening, so it was likely depleted. Employee remade sanitizer. A concentration of 200ppm Cl was observed.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Mop bucket near was observed containing dirty mop water from the night before. Ensure dirty mop water is discarded after use to reduce pest harborage. Place mops so that they will air dry.
6-501.114: The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 A certified food manager was not present at the time of inspection. Store manager has been registered to take a food manager course for certification since the routine inspection on 11/15/22. Ensure enough staff complete the food manager certification course to allow for the presence of a certified food manager during all hours of operation. 
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of food handler certification was not available for one of the employees working at the time of inspection. Completion of food safety training is required as part of onboarding process prior to working at the facility. Ensure copies of certifications are available for all staff that are not certified food managers. See general comments for additional information.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed for handwashing, sanitization, and proper use of chemicals. Staff were not aware the sanitizer dispenser was not working properly (see General Comments for additional information). Also, PIC at the facility is not a certified food manager. The one certified food manager that was on-site for Road Ranger had to leave for the day. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at the followup inspection.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 A certified food manager was not present at the time of inspection. Store manager has not yet completed the food manager certification. The assistant manager currently has a food handler certification. The Road Ranger manager with a food manager certification had to leave the facility for the day. Ensure enough staff complete the food manager certification course to allow for the presence of a certified food manager during all hours of operation. 
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to dispensing paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Ensure proper handwashing between tasks. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.11 Store manager was observed walking around with a disposable wiping cloth tucked in their apron and at one point was observed wiping their hands on the towel. The towel was discarded when manager left for the afternoon. Proper use of wiping cloths and handwashing were discussed with assistant manager. The disposable wiping cloths are not intended to be used for wiping hands. If hands need to be wiped then they should be washed. 
Food employees shall keep their hands and exposed portions of their arms clean.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Empty sani-bucket was observed sitting in the basin of the back handwashing sink. Sani-bucket was removed from the sink. Proper use of handwashing sinks was discussed. Do not place anything in the basins of handwashing sinks, and ensure handwashing sinks are not used as dump sinks. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat sanitizer was observed at 100ppm in freshly dispensed solutions for the 3 part sink and sani-bucket. After adjusting the water temperature a few times the solution was still not dispensing at proper concentration. A call for service is needed. In the meantime, the quat solution was mixed manually to provide solutions at 200ppm. Ensure test strips are used to verify concentration of quat solutions. The effective concentration range for the product in use is 150-400ppm. Aim for 200ppm when preparing solutions. The dispenser cannot be used to prepare quat solutions until it is repaired and working properly. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-202.12 & 7-102.11 Bright blue liquid in an unlabeled spray bottle was said to be sanitizer. Product tested at a concentration off the chart for quat product. Staff were unsure as to what exactly was used to make the solution. Liquid was discarded. If this was sanitizer it was too strong. Ensure proper use of toxics and that all bottles are properly labeled.
Toxics shall be used according to the manufacturer's use directions included in labeling, and must not be used in a manner that poses a health hazard or potential risk of cross contamination.
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Empty sani-bucket was observed in the basin of the back handwashing sink. Sanitizer was manually mixed to provide solution at 200ppm. Ensure sanitizer solution is always available for use. When one solution is emptied another should be prepared in its place.
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of food handler certifications were not available for the store manager or another employee that arrived for their shift during the inspection. The assistant manager was able to show proof of their certification via their cellphone. Ensure copies of food handler certifications are available for all staff. Ensure all staff that are not certified food managers complete an online food handler certification course within 30 days of hiring, and maintain copies of certifications on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Facility manager and employee working at the time of inspection did not have signed employee health policy forms on file. Employee health policy was discussed, and forms were signed during inspection. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to dispensing paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed, and employee was observed washing hands with proper technique for the remainder of inspection. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted at the front handwashing sink. Handwashing sign was provided and posted at the handwashing sink. 
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.citation_text:
3-403.11 Meatballs in hot baine were observed with surface and internal temperatures of 109F-117F and 114F-125F respectively. Meatballs were just heated in the microwave for hot holding prior to inspector’s arrival. Internal temperature was not verified prior to hot holding. Reheating for hot holding was discussed. Meatballs were portioned and cold held since Saturday and needed to be heated to at least 165F prior to service. Meatballs were reheated to 167F prior to hot holding. 
Ready to eat, TCS food that has been commercially processed and packaged in a food processing plant that is inspected by the regulatory authority that has jurisdiction over the plant, shall be heated to a temperature of at least 135F when being reheated for hot holding.  Any portions held cold after removed from original packaging and heated at a later time need to reach an internal temperature of at least 165F.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Shelves in walk-in cooler had varying amounts of general buildup and mold. Shelving unit with the most buildup was in the back left corner. Manager noted staff are in the process of cleaning all shelving in the walk-in cooler.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114 Quat sanitizer was at ~100ppm after being freshly dispensed for sani-bucket used on gas station side. Subway 3 part sink observed with a concentration less than 100ppm. The lid on the chemical suction line that seals to the jug was broken. A part needs to be ordered to replace the line. Arrow Chemical Products Sanitizer (effective concentration 200-400ppm) was available and used to make solutions. Concentration observed at 200-400ppn for fresh solutions. Spot check will be done to check function of quat dispenser after part is replaced.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12 Infrared thermometer was the only type of thermometer available for checking food temperatures. Attachable probe was available on gas station side. Subway will utilize the probe from gas station until a replacement probe is purchased. NOTE: Gas station is limiting food service and does not use the probe daily at this time. However, ensure a probe food thermometer is available for both permitted areas.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 PIC with food manager certification had to leave prior to conclusion of inspection. The person left in charge only had a food handler certification. Additional staff with food manager certifications are needed. Ensure that enough staff have food manager certifications to allow for a designated person in charge with a CFM to be present during all hours of operation (see general comments for details).
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to prepare an order after working the cash register. Handwashing between tasks was discussed. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands, such as handling money, and before putting on gloves/between glove changes.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted at the handsink up front by the make line. Maintain handwashing signage at all designated handsinks. Handwashing signs were provided for management to post where needed. 
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwasing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution at 3 part sink for ware washing was observed at 100ppm. Effective concentration per product label is 150-400ppm A freshly dispensed bucket to be used on the gas station side was observed at 0ppm. Upon rerunning the solution the concentration was observed at 200ppm. Ensure the temperature of the water used to make sanitizer is cool to warm and not too hot, as the temperature can effect the concentration. Use test strips to verify concentration when making solutions. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Spray bottle containing a purple chemical with a worn label that appeared to say lime away was observed in the dish area. PIC thought it was degreaser. Product was discarded. Ensure proper labeling on working supplies of chemicals.
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11 Bag of onions was observed on the floor in the walkin cooler. Ensure foods are stored properly. 
Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor in a clean, dry location where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 A disposable wiping cloth previously used for wiping down tables was being reused for wiping down the back prep table and was not stored properly. The wiping cloth was previously used with sanitizer dispensed from a spray bottle, and sani-bucket with quat solution was not available for storing cloth between uses. Wiping cloth was discarded. Proper storage of wiping cloths in solution between uses and/or immediate discard when used with spray bottles of sanitizer were discussed.
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-501.18 Sanitizer solution in-use at knife caddy on the make line was observed to be visibly soiled. Knives were also observed stored in the solution and not the side compartment. Proper storage of knives after wiping was discussed. The knife sanitizer caddy was cleaned and provided with new solution at 200ppm. Ensure caddy is cleaned/sanitized and provided with fresh solution for wiping knifes as needed when soil buildup occurs and/or up to every 4hrs after continuous use. 
Chemical sanitizing solutions shall be clean.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11  Floor tiles were loose and damaged between the grease trap and the floor drain under the 3 part sink.
--Baseboard tiles were damaged and/or missing by the back door and on the left side of the water heater.
Provide proper repairs in the aforementioned areas.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.16 Damp mop was observed in mop bucket. Ensure proper storage of damp mops between uses. 
After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment or supplies.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-160 Observed an unopened stack of coffee cup lids stored directly beneath the frontline handsink plumbing lines and adjacent to the mouse bait. Lids were discarded during the inspection. Discussed the proper storage of lids and other facility materials under plumbing lines. Make sure that the storage of utensils and equipment remains away from directly beneath plumbing.  Food and equipment shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 750-820d Observed the sani-bucket being used to wipe the probe thermometer between uses to test at 100ppm Quat. It was discovered that the wall-mounted dispensing bucket was empty of chemical product. Product bucket was replaced with a fresh and full bucket. A new sanitizing solution was created within the sani-bucket. This solution tested at 200ppm Quat. Educate staff on proper testing of solution concentration before use. Make sure that staff is aware of how the system works and to glance at the volume remaining in chemical bucket prior to use.  Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in accordance to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Observed the cloth being used to wipe the probe thermometer between uses to be stored on the counter. Store cloth within sani-solution between uses to insure that cloth is being sanitized. Cloth was placed in solution during the inspection. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment: 750-1160 Observed mouse droppings in the cabinet beneath the drive thru soda dispenser (older droppings.green from bait) and within the opened closet by the back door. This closet has become a catch for maintenance and various other sundry items. This closet is also stocked with bottle beverages so that seeing the floor is difficult. Shelving has been ordered and will be arriving within the week. Shelving will help keep the bottle off the floor. Clean the floor within this closet. Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1200 REPEAT: The coving to the right of the hot holding unit is observed peeling from the wall. Properly seal the base cove to the wall to eliminate areas for crumbs to accumulate and possibly become a food source for pests.   The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1210 Observed a hole in the wall to the right of the island preparation cooler/hot holding side. The hole looks like it was created in order to run cable. Seal up the wall as much as possible and allow minimal space for wiring. All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800(b) The soda  nozzles of the drive-thru dispenser are observed soiled with accumulated syrup and soil debris. Clean the nozzles and the underside of the label displays. To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e The cabinet beneath the handsink behind the cash register is observed soiled with chemical stains and water marks. Clean the interior of the cabinet. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: 750-880 The black caddy holding cups and lids by the drive thru is observed soiled with dust and minute food crumbs. Clean the caddy so that single-service items are maintained clean. Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1200 REPEAT: There is a piece of tile coving missing from the right side of the back door. Replace the coving. The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch. ALSO, the floor drain in the walk-in cooler is observed soiled with accumulated mold. Clean the floor drain.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1220  Observed a wave of mold on the ceiling of the walk-in cooler. Clean the ceiling and possibly the right side of the walk-in by the bread holder. Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.
